title: 3D Benchy
desc: The 3D Benchy is the world's most-printed 3D model and the standard torture test for FDM printers. Designed by Creative Tools, this little tugboat packs overhangs, bridging, curved surfaces, small details, and symmetry checks into one 60mm print. Every new printer, filament, or slicer profile gets validated against a Benchy: stringing shows in the cabin windows, overhang droop on the bow, elephant's foot at the hull base, and layer consistency along the hull. It is the universal benchmark print — if your Benchy is clean, your printer is dialed in. Designer: Creative Tools. License: CC BY. Group: calibration. Year: 2015. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA (standard); PETG for functional tests.

title: 20mm XYZ Calibration Cube
desc: The 20mm XYZ calibration cube is the simplest dimensional-accuracy test in 3D printing. A hollow-free 20x20x20mm cube with embossed X, Y, and Z letters lets you verify each axis with calipers: every face should measure 20.00mm within 0.1mm. Skewed dimensions reveal belt tension problems, wrong steps-per-mm, or frame squareness issues. Print it in 20 minutes, measure all three axes, and adjust before committing to long prints. Every printer owner should keep a reference cube from each machine. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: calibration. Year: 2016. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Cali Cat
desc: Cali Cat is a cute calibration cat that tests overhangs, bridging, stringing, and fine detail in one friendly 35mm print. Its tail is a steep overhang, the ears test small-feature cooling, and the whisker gaps reveal stringing. Faster and more fun than a cube, it is the go-to first print for dialing in a new filament: one cat per temperature step builds a visual temperature tower of quality. The model prints without supports and finishes in under an hour. Designer: Dezign. License: Open license (community). Group: calibration. Year: 2017. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Temperature Tower
desc: A temperature tower prints the same test geometry at stepped temperatures (e.g., 220C down to 185C in 5C blocks) so you can read the optimal nozzle temperature for any filament off the finished print. Each block is labeled with its temperature; look for the cleanest bridging, sharpest overhangs, and least stringing. This single 2-hour print replaces days of trial and error and is the correct first step with every new spool. G-code post-processing scripts in most slicers automate the temperature changes. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: calibration. Year: 2016. Parts: 1. Materials: Any filament under test.

title: Retraction Test (Twin Towers)
desc: The twin-tower retraction test prints two thin pillars with a gap between them, forcing dozens of travel moves. Stringing, blobs, or wisps between the towers reveal retraction distance and speed problems. Tune retraction in 0.5mm steps until the gap is clean. This 15-minute print saves hours of post-processing on real models and is essential when switching between PLA, PETG (stringier), and TPU (minimal retraction). Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: calibration. Year: 2017. Parts: 1. Materials: Filament under test.

title: Voron 2.4 Printed Parts Set
desc: The Voron 2.4 is a flagship open-source CoreXY 3D printer, and its entire printed-parts set — 87 components including the StealthBurner toolhead, TAP probe mount, gantry joints, and skirt pieces — is released under the GPL. These are functional engineering parts, not decorations: they must be printed in ABS or ASA with high infill for heat resistance inside the enclosed chamber (60C+ ambient). This set is the definitive advanced print project: 60+ hours of printing that ends with a 350mm^3 high-speed printer. The Voron project proves open hardware can outperform commercial machines. Designer: VoronDesign. License: GPL. Group: mechanical. Year: 2020. Parts: 87. Materials: ABS or ASA (enclosure required).

title: Prusa i3 MK3S+ Printed Parts
desc: Prusa Research prints its own printer parts: the i3 MK3S+ ships with 30+ 3D-printed PETG components (extruder body, X-ends, Y-corners, LCD cover) that Prusa manufactures on its 500+ printer farm in Prague. The STLs are GPL, so anyone can print spares or build a full MK3S+ from the open BOM. PETG is specified for its layer adhesion and temperature resistance. This is the canonical example of 3D printing as real manufacturing — a farm of printers literally reproducing themselves. Designer: Prusa Research. License: GPL. Group: mechanical. Year: 2019. Parts: 30. Materials: PETG (Prusa Galaxy Black).

title: StealthBurner Toolhead
desc: The StealthBurner is VoronDesign's GPL toolhead for Voron printers: a compact direct-drive extruder with dual 5015 part-cooling fans, Clockwork 2 extruder gears, and an integrated TAP or inductive probe mount. Its 12 printed parts form ducted airflow that cools bridges and overhangs at 300mm/s+ print speeds. As a standalone project it teaches duct design, fan shrouds, and heat management — skills that transfer to any printer mod. Print in ABS/ASA; PLA will soften near the heater block. Designer: VoronDesign. License: GPL. Group: mechanical. Year: 2022. Parts: 12. Materials: ABS or ASA.

title: Gridfinity Baseplate System
desc: Gridfinity is Zack Freedman's open modular organization system: a 42x42mm grid baseplate with stackable bins in 1x1 to 6x6 unit sizes, all parametric in OpenSCAD. Print baseplates for your drawers and bins for every component — screws, SD cards, tools — and everything snaps into a perfect grid. The system went viral because it solves the universal maker problem: chaotic parts drawers. Baseplates print flat without supports; bins print in vase-friendly walls. Scale the grid to any drawer in the parametric files. Designer: Zack Freedman. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2022. Parts: 3. Materials: PLA.

title: E-NABLE Phoenix Prosthetic Hand
desc: The e-NABLE Phoenix hand is an open-source 3D-printed prosthetic for below-elbow limb differences, designed by the global e-NABLE volunteer community. Body-powered: wrist flexion drives finger closure through tension cords, giving a functional grip for under $50 in filament versus thousands for commercial devices. Over 10,000 hands have been delivered free to recipients worldwide. Print in PLA with 30%+ infill for strength; assembly needs screws, elastic cord, and padding. This is 3D printing at its most meaningful — volunteers manufacturing medical devices for strangers. Designer: e-NABLE Community. License: Open license (community). Group: assistive. Year: 2014. Parts: 30. Materials: PLA (30%+ infill for strength).

title: Montana Mask Frame
desc: The Montana Mask is an open-source 3D-printed respirator frame designed by Dr. Dusty Richardson during the 2020 PPE shortage. It holds a square of surgical mask or furnace-filter material in a sealed frame with a printed filter grille, giving a reusable N95-style seal. Hospitals, makerspaces, and individuals printed hundreds of thousands. The 2-part print takes 3 hours in PLA or PETG; filter material and elastic complete it. A landmark case of distributed emergency manufacturing via desktop 3D printing. Designer: Dr. Dusty Richardson. License: Open license (community). Group: assistive. Year: 2020. Parts: 2. Materials: PLA or PETG.

title: Articulated Crystal Dragon
desc: Cinderwing3D's articulated crystal dragon is the iconic print-in-place flexi toy: dozens of interlocking segments print already assembled, flexing like a real spine straight off the bed. No supports, no assembly — the clearances are engineered into the model. It demonstrates advanced tolerance design (0.3-0.5mm gaps that print separately but stay linked). A perfect showpiece print that proves your printer's dimensional accuracy and makes an unbeatable gift. Print slow with good cooling for crisp segment separation. Designer: Cinderwing3D. License: CC BY-NC. Group: toys. Year: 2021. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA (silk PLA looks best).

title: Lithophane Photo Panel
desc: A lithophane is a 3D-printed photo: varying the thickness of white PLA (0.8mm to 3mm) encodes image brightness, so the picture appears when backlit. Free lithophane makers convert any photo to a curved or flat STL in seconds. Print in white PLA at 0.1mm layers, 100% infill, standing vertical for best resolution. The result looks like magic — a blank white slab that reveals a portrait in window light. Popular for nightlights, ornaments, and memorial pieces. Designer: Open community technique. License: Public domain (technique). Group: art. Year: 2018. Parts: 1. Materials: White PLA (100% infill).

title: Cable Chain (Energy Chain)
desc: Print-in-place cable chains route wires cleanly on 3D printers, CNC machines, and robots. Each link snaps to the next with engineered clearances, forming a flexible chain that guides cables through a controlled bend radius. Print 20+ links flat, snap together, and mount with printed brackets. Sizing is parametric: link inner width must clear your cable bundle plus 20%. A rite-of-passage functional print that makes any machine look professional and protects wiring from fatigue. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: mechanical. Year: 2018. Parts: 20. Materials: PETG (flexible, durable).

title: Filament Dry Box
desc: Wet filament causes popping, stringing, and weak layers — a dry box fixes it. This printed 6-part design converts a cereal container into a sealed spool holder with PTFE feed tubes, desiccant trays, and a hygrometer window. Print in PETG (moisture resistant), add a $3 cereal container and silica gel, and your nylon/PETG/TPU stays under 20% humidity indefinitely. Essential for anyone printing hygroscopic filaments; pays for itself in saved failed prints. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 6. Materials: PETG.

title: Parametric Battery Dispenser
desc: A gravity-feed AA/AAA battery dispenser: load fresh batteries at the top, pull dead ones from the bottom slot. The parametric OpenSCAD source adjusts to any battery size. Three printed parts (body, ramp, front plate) assemble without hardware. Print in PLA with 15% infill; the design uses printed rails instead of fasteners. A perfect first functional print — useful daily, impossible to buy this exact size, and demonstrates parametric design thinking. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 3. Materials: PLA.

title: Tool Holder Wall Panel
desc: Modular wall panels with printed hooks, bins, and holders turn any workshop wall into organized storage. The 8-part starter set includes hex-key holders, screwdriver racks, spool mounts, and parts bins that friction-fit into slotted panels. Panels tile to cover any wall area; print more hooks as your tool collection grows. PLA is fine indoors; use PETG near windows (UV). A weekend project that permanently upgrades a workspace. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 8. Materials: PLA (PETG near windows).

title: Self-Watering Planter
desc: A 3-part self-watering planter: outer pot, inner soil basket, and water reservoir with a wicking cord. Fill the reservoir monthly; capillary action waters the plant. Print in PETG (water-resistant) with 3+ walls to prevent seepage, and seal the reservoir with food-safe epoxy if needed. The design scales parametrically from succulent pots to herb planters. Combines 3D printing with real horticulture — a living functional print. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2021. Parts: 3. Materials: PETG (water resistant).

title: Cookie Cutter Set
desc: Custom cookie cutters are the classic personalized print: any silhouette becomes a cutter in minutes with free generators. This 5-shape starter set prints with a reinforced 0.8mm cutting edge and comfortable handle. Use food-safe PLA and hand-wash only (layer lines harbor bacteria; never dishwasher). Design your own from any black-and-white image — wedding shapes, logos, pet silhouettes. A 30-minute print that makes every holiday better. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2018. Parts: 5. Materials: Food-safe PLA.

title: Phone Stand (Adjustable)
desc: A 2-part adjustable phone stand with indexed tilt angles from 30 to 75 degrees. The base prints flat, the cradle snaps in with detents — no hardware, no glue. Fits phones with cases up to 12mm thick; the parametric source scales to tablets. Print in PLA with 20% infill; add adhesive rubber feet to stop sliding. The canonical desk-upgrade print: 2 hours, infinitely more useful than the factory box your phone came in. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2019. Parts: 2. Materials: PLA.

title: Headphone Stand
desc: A single-piece headphone stand with a wide stable base and curved yoke that cradles the headband without compressing ear pads. Prints without supports in 4 hours; the yoke's 40mm radius fits over-ear headphones from all major brands. Add felt pads to the yoke to protect leather headbands. Variants include under-desk clamp mounts and dual-headset stands. The definitive desk-tidiness print — cheap, fast, and used every single day. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2019. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Drawer Organizer Grid
desc: Interlocking drawer organizer trays in 6 sizes that tile any drawer with zero wasted space. Each tray prints flat in 2 hours; dovetail edges lock trays together so they never shift. The parametric source regenerates trays to exact millimeter dimensions — measure once, print a perfect fit. Use PLA for desk drawers, PETG for kitchen (heat/steam). Replaces $40 store organizers with $2 of filament cut exactly to your drawers. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 6. Materials: PLA (PETG for kitchen).

title: SD Card Holder
desc: A pocket-size holder for 8 micro-SD cards with labeled slots and a snap-fit lid. Prints in 45 minutes with 0.15mm layers for crisp slot tolerances; cards press in with a satisfying click and never fall out in a bag. Essential for photographers, drone pilots, and Raspberry Pi users juggling a dozen cards. Print in bright colors so it never gets lost in a gear bag. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2018. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Raspberry Pi 4 Case
desc: A 3-part ventilated case for the Raspberry Pi 4 with GPIO slot, camera ribbon cutout, and 30mm fan mount. The Pi 4 throttles under load without cooling — this case's chimney vents and optional fan keep it at full clock indefinitely. Prints in 3 hours; brass inserts or printed threads take the M2.5 screws. Dozens of variants exist (stackable, DIN-rail, touchscreen), but this vented 3-piece is the reliable standard every Pi owner should print first. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: educational. Year: 2019. Parts: 3. Materials: PLA (PETG near heat).

title: Spool Holder with Bearings
desc: A low-friction spool holder using 608 skate bearings: the spool spins freely, eliminating extruder strain and under-extrusion on heavy 1kg spools. Four printed parts (2 arms, axle, base) plus two 608 bearings assemble in minutes. Mounts to 2020 extrusion or sits on a desk. The bearing upgrade matters — a dragging spool causes inconsistent extrusion that looks exactly like a clogged nozzle. Every printer benefits; total cost under $3. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2018. Parts: 4. Materials: PLA.

title: Hex Key Organizer
desc: A single-piece organizer with labeled holes for every hex key from 1.5mm to 10mm. Holes are sized +0.2mm over nominal for a friction fit that holds keys upside-down but releases with a pull. Print at 0.15mm layers for accurate holes. Mounts to pegboard or sits on a bench. Ends the eternal hunt for the 2.5mm key — the one your printer actually needs — by giving every key a labeled home. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Vase (Spiral Mode)
desc: Spiral (vase) mode prints a vase as one continuous extrusion — a single 0.8mm wall spiraling upward with zero layer seams, zero infill, zero retractions. The result is a watertight, translucent-feeling vessel in 3 hours. Hundreds of parametric vase profiles exist (twisted, ribbed, faceted); all share the technique. Use PLA or PETG; translucent filament with a tea light inside is stunning. Teaches the single most elegant slicer trick: one wall, one spiral, one beautiful object. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: art. Year: 2017. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA or translucent PETG.

title: Soap Dish with Drainage
desc: A 2-part soap dish with sloped drainage channels and a drip tray that keeps bar soap dry and lasting twice as long. The dish lifts the bar on ribs; water drains to the tray below. Print in PETG (bathroom humidity/heat) with 20% infill. Dishwasher-safe at low temp if printed in PETG. A small print with outsized daily impact — soggy soap is a solved problem. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2019. Parts: 2. Materials: PETG (bathroom humidity).

title: Toothbrush Holder
desc: A wall-mount toothbrush holder with ventilated slots that keep brushes separated and air-drying. Four slots fit manual and electric heads; drainage holes prevent water pooling. Print in PETG and mount with Command strips — no drilling. The ventilated design matters: enclosed holders grow mildew; open printed slots stay clean. A 2-hour print that beats every store holder on hygiene. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2018. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG.

title: Wall Shelf Brackets
desc: Parametric shelf brackets that hold 12mm plywood or pine boards — print 4 brackets, buy a board, get a shelf. Each bracket takes 4 wall screws and is rated by the community for 5kg+ per pair when printed in PETG with 40% infill. The parametric file adjusts depth and board thickness. Stronger than expected: printed brackets with proper infill and wall count rival bent-steel brackets for light shelving. Print, mount to studs, drop in the board. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 4. Materials: PETG (40% infill for strength).

title: Drill Bit Index Case
desc: A hinged index case with labeled holes for a full 29-piece drill bit set (1/16 to 1/2 by 64ths). The lid prints with living-hinge geometry or separate pin hinges; bit holes are stepped so each bit sits at labeled depth. Print the case flat in 6 hours. Ends the coffee-can-of-bits era: every bit visible, labeled, and protected from chipping. The labeling alone saves ten minutes per project. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 2. Materials: PLA.

title: Filament Swatch Kit
desc: Printed color swatches — small labeled chips of every filament you own — beat photos for judging real color and finish. This 20-swatch starter kit includes a storage ring; each swatch prints in 10 minutes with your standard profile, labeled by filament brand and color. When a project needs 'that perfect red,' flip through physical swatches instead of guessing from a screen. Makers with 30+ spools swear by the system. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2020. Parts: 20. Materials: Each filament sampled.

title: Enclosure Door Handle
desc: A chunky 2-part handle for Lack-table or custom printer enclosures, sized for gloved hands and printed in ASA for heat resistance. The handle bridges a 200mm span with internal ribs — strong enough to yank a warped acrylic door open. Includes mounting blocks with heat-set inserts. Small part, big ergonomics: stock enclosure doors have nowhere to grab. Print in ASA/ABS to survive 60C chamber heat. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2021. Parts: 2. Materials: ASA (heat resistant).

title: Lead Screw Cover
desc: Telescoping covers that shield Z lead screws from dust and filament debris — the grit that causes Z-banding and premature nut wear. Two printed tubes slide over each other as the gantry moves. Print in PLA, 0.2mm, no supports; size to your screw diameter +2mm. A 2-hour print that extends lead screw life indefinitely and visibly smooths Z motion on dusty-shop printers. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: mechanical. Year: 2019. Parts: 2. Materials: PLA.

title: Toolhead Cable Strain Relief
desc: A printed strain-relief clamp that anchors the toolhead cable bundle, stopping the flex-fatigue breaks that kill thermistor and heater wires mid-print. The clamp's ribbed jaws grip the cable sleeve without crushing wires; it bolts to standard toolhead plates. Fifteen minutes to print, five to install, and it eliminates the most common electrical failure on fast CoreXY machines. Print in PETG for heat and flex resistance. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: mechanical. Year: 2020. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG.

title: Dry-Erase Board Clips
desc: Clips that mount a whiteboard sheet to any wall with Command strips — a $15 whiteboard for the price of filament. Four corner clips grip 3mm board stock; the parametric file fits any sheet size. Print in PLA, stick to the wall, slide in the board. Perfect for workshop task lists, kids' rooms, and Kanban boards. The clips' spring geometry is a nice lesson in printed flexures. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2021. Parts: 4. Materials: PLA.

title: Garden Hose Guide
desc: Spiked guides that stake into lawn edges and keep garden hoses from crushing flower beds. The 2-part design (stake + roller) lets the hose glide around corners instead of dragging through petunias. Print in PETG or ASA for UV resistance — PLA gets brittle in sun within a season. Stake every 2 meters along bed edges. A 1-hour print per guide that saves the garden. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 2. Materials: PETG or ASA (UV resistant).

title: Shower Head Holder
desc: A suction-cup shower head holder that repositions the spray anywhere on tile — no drilling, no landlord issues. The printed socket grips standard 22mm shower wands; a heavy-duty suction cup (hardware store) provides the mount. Print in PETG for steam resistance. Holds 2kg+ when the cup is properly seated on clean tile. Renters' favorite functional print. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2019. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG (steam resistant).

title: Keychain Bottle Opener
desc: A keychain bottle opener with a printed lever and embedded coin edge — the classic 'my printer is useful' demo. The trick is 100% infill and 4+ walls: printed PLA at full density opens bottles reliably. Print flat in 30 minutes, add a split ring. Makes great party favors and proves to skeptics that printed parts handle real loads. (Metal coin insert optional for heavy users.) Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2018. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA (100% infill).

title: Desk Cable Grommet
desc: A 2-piece grommet that finishes a 60mm desk cable hole with brush bristles to hide cables while passing plugs. Print the ring and cap; add cheap brush strip from the hardware store. The parametric file fits any hole saw size. Turns a ragged drilled hole into a professional cable port in one 1-hour print. Essential for standing-desk cable management. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Bird Feeder
desc: A 4-part hanging bird feeder with seed tray, roof, perch ring, and hanger. The roof's 45-degree overhang prints support-free; drainage holes in the tray keep seed dry. Print in PETG or ASA for outdoor UV survival — PLA warps in summer sun. Hang from a branch and watch the visitors. A family-friendly weekend print that turns a backyard into a nature show. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2020. Parts: 4. Materials: PETG or ASA (outdoor).

title: Compost Bin Latch
desc: A replacement latch for compost bins whose factory clasps always break first. The 2-part printed latch (hook + catch) fits standard bin rims and survives years of outdoor use in ASA. Measure your bin's rim profile, print, and snap in — no tools. The perfect 'repair don't replace' print: a $0.30 part saves a $60 bin from landfill. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2021. Parts: 2. Materials: ASA (outdoor UV/heat).

title: Vacuum Hose Adapter
desc: Adapters between mismatched vacuum hose diameters — the universal workshop print. Measure both hose IDs, generate the stepped adapter parametrically, print in PETG. Every shop has the problem: new tool, wrong hose size. A 2-hour print replaces a $25 specialty adapter and a week of waiting. Keep the parametric file handy; you'll use it monthly. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG.

title: Dust Shoe for CNC
desc: A 3-part dust shoe that surrounds a CNC spindle with brush bristles and a vacuum port, capturing 95% of chips at the cut. The shoe floats on the Z axis with printed springs; bristles conform to the workpiece. Print in PETG (dust + vibration). Pair with the vacuum hose adapter above for a complete dust system. Transforms CNC routing from a dust storm into a clean operation. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2020. Parts: 3. Materials: PETG.

title: Soldering Helping Hands
desc: Articulated alligator-clip arms on a weighted base for holding wires and PCBs while soldering. Five printed parts plus alligator clips and ball-joint hardware; the arms pose and stay put. Print in PETG (near a hot iron). A must for electronics work — third and fourth hands that never shake. Assembly teaches ball-joint design and printed threads. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: educational. Year: 2019. Parts: 5. Materials: PETG (near hot iron).

title: Multimeter Stand
desc: A tilt stand that holds your multimeter at bench-viewing angle with probe holders on the sides. The single-piece print has a 60-degree face and cable management slot. Fits standard handheld DMM footprints; the parametric file adjusts width. Print in PLA, 20% infill. Stops the meter sliding off the bench and puts the display where you can read it while probing with both hands. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2020. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Oscilloscope Probe Holder
desc: A bench holder with spring clips for 4 oscilloscope probes, keeping $200 probes off the bench and untangled. The clips are printed flexures sized to probe barrels — firm grip, easy release. Mount to a shelf edge or bench back. Print in PETG for clip fatigue life. Cheap insurance for expensive test gear. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2021. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG (clip fatigue life).

title: Wire Spool Rack
desc: A 6-part rack holding 4 wire spools on a rotating dowel with a cutter bar. Pull wire to length, press against the cutter, done. The frame prints flat; a wooden dowel carries the spools. Sized for common 1lb electronics spools. Turns a tangled wire drawer into a dispensing station. Print in PLA; the cutter is a replaceable razor blade in a printed guard. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2019. Parts: 6. Materials: PLA.

title: Parts Washer Basket
desc: A perforated basket sized for ultrasonic cleaners and IPA wash stations — drop resin prints or small parts in, lift out clean. The 3mm perforations drain solvent while retaining parts down to M3 screws. Print in PETG (IPA resistant; PLA softens in IPA). A 3-hour print that upgrades every wash station from 'tweezers and hope' to professional workflow. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2021. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG (IPA resistant).

title: Resin Vat Drip Stand
desc: A 2-part stand that holds a resin printer build plate at draining angle over the vat — no more dripping resin across the machine. The angled cradle fits standard plate sizes; resin flows back into the vat instead of onto your bench. Print in PETG (resin-resistant). Five minutes of printing saves endless cleanup and wasted resin on every resin print job. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2020. Parts: 2. Materials: PETG (resin resistant).

title: Chess Set (Staunton)
desc: A full 32-piece Staunton chess set — the public-domain 1849 Nathaniel Cook design, the tournament standard. Each piece prints in 1-2 hours; a full set is a 40-hour marathon that teaches supports (knights), fine detail (pawns), and patience. Print in two colors or stain one side. Weighted bases (glue in washers) give tournament feel. The classic long-print project: start Friday, play Sunday. Designer: Open community design. License: Public domain (Staunton design 1849). Group: toys. Year: 2019. Parts: 32. Materials: PLA (two colors).

title: Fidget Cube Gears
desc: A 6-gear fidget toy where meshed planetary gears spin silently in a printed frame. The gear teeth are generated parametrically — correct involute-ish profiles that actually mesh. Prints in 3 hours with 0.15mm layers for smooth teeth; a drop of lubricant makes it whisper-quiet. Demonstrates gear geometry you can hold: turn one gear and watch the ratio cascade. Great desk toy and better gear-theory lesson. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: toys. Year: 2018. Parts: 6. Materials: PLA.

title: Marble Run Track Set
desc: A 24-piece modular marble run: straights, curves, funnels, and drops that friction-fit into towers of any height. Standard 16mm marbles; the track gauge is parametric. Kids learn gravity, momentum, and iteration — rebuild the run ten ways in an afternoon. Print in bright PLA, 15% infill; a full set is 20 hours of printing for years of play. The ultimate family print project. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: toys. Year: 2020. Parts: 24. Materials: PLA (bright colors).

title: Bathroom Tile Spacer
desc: Reusable 3mm tile spacers — print 20 in 30 minutes instead of buying bags of single-use plastic. The X-profile spacers set grout lines evenly and pull out cleanly before grout sets. Print in PLA; they survive a whole bathroom and then recycle. A tiny print with real renovation economics: $0.50 of filament replaces $15 of spacers. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2021. Parts: 20. Materials: PLA.

title: Paint Rack (Dropper Bottles)
desc: A 4-tier rack holding 48 dropper bottles (Vallejo/Citadel size) at label-forward angle for miniature painters. Each tier prints flat; tiers stack with printed pins. The 30-degree tilt shows every label at a glance — no more digging through a box for 'that one green.' Print in PLA, any color; a full rack is 12 hours. The miniature-painting community's favorite organization print. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: art. Year: 2020. Parts: 4. Materials: PLA.

title: Miniature Terrain (28mm)
desc: An 8-piece 28mm tabletop terrain set: ruined walls, crates, barricades, and scatter — everything for a skirmish board. Prints at 0.15mm for crisp detail; dry-brush painting brings out the stonework. Scale-accurate to standard miniature games. A full table is 30+ hours of printing, but each piece is a satisfying evening print. The gateway from printing to tabletop gaming. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: toys. Year: 2019. Parts: 8. Materials: PLA.

title: Greenhouse Vent Opener Bracket
desc: A bracket adapting automatic wax-cylinder vent openers to hobby greenhouses — the opener pushes the vent open as temperature rises, no electricity. The printed bracket bridges the opener's stroke to standard vent frames. Print in ASA (greenhouse heat + UV). Set-and-forget climate control: the vent breathes with the day. Gardeners call it the best $5 upgrade in the hobby. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: household. Year: 2021. Parts: 2. Materials: ASA (greenhouse heat/UV).

title: Rain Gauge
desc: A 2-part rain gauge with molded millimeter scale — print, mount on a fence post, read rainfall to the millimeter. The funnel's 100mm collection diameter matches standard gauge geometry so readings compare with official stations. Print in translucent PETG to read the level without opening. A perfect classroom print: students track weather, graph data, and learn measurement. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: educational. Year: 2020. Parts: 2. Materials: Translucent PETG.

title: Sundial (Latitude-Specific)
desc: A horizontal sundial with the gnomon angled to YOUR latitude — generated parametrically, correct hour lines for your location. Print flat in 4 hours; the gnomon's angle equals latitude, so shadows tell true solar time. Add a compass rose base. Ancient timekeeping, parametric precision: enter latitude, print, place in sun, read time. A stunning garden piece and a real astronomy lesson. Designer: Open community design. License: Public domain (gnomonics). Group: educational. Year: 2019. Parts: 1. Materials: PETG or ASA (outdoor).

title: Anemometer Cups
desc: Replacement cups for a DIY anemometer: 3 hemispherical cups on printed arms spinning a hall-effect sensor. Print cups in PETG (balanced, weatherproof); the rotor geometry is the classic 3-cup design with known calibration (wind speed ≈ 2.5 × rotation rate). Pair with an Arduino for a complete weather station. Students build real meteorology instruments for dollars. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: educational. Year: 2021. Parts: 4. Materials: PETG (weatherproof).

title: 3D Printer Volumetric Slice Coordinates
desc: Stratified layer-by-layer toolpaths and thermal extrusion profiles for additive manufacturing. Slice data converts a 3D model into the precise moves and temperatures a printer executes. Key aspects include: Layer height trades print time against surface quality; Toolpaths include perimeters, infill, and support structures; Extrusion profiles match temperature and flow to the material; Z-seam placement keeps visible artifacts consistent; Estimated print time derives from path lengths and speeds (estimate, not a validated print job). title: 3D Printing G-Code Layer Profiles
desc: Extruder thermal curves, fan speed overrides, volumetric flow rates, and infill pattern paths for additive manufacturing, expressed as complete 3D printing G-code layer profiles. Each profile is a usable starting configuration: temperatures, speeds, and paths a printer can execute directly. Displayed print times are slicer estimates, not validated print jobs — wall thickness, supports, nozzle settings, printer motion limits, and material-specific slicing all change real results. Key aspects include: Thermal curves stage nozzle and bed temperatures per material; Fan speed overrides balance cooling against layer adhesion; Volumetric flow caps prevent extruder skipping; Infill patterns trade part strength for print time; Actual directions: slice the model, verify first-layer adhesion, and run a temperature tower before committing to the full print.
